clue.text: Lay egg or develop grotesque figure

indicators.note: to develop something is to work it into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice between laying an egg or growing into some grotesque creature, like a fairy-tale curse.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargoyle is a carved monster on a church roof, the classic example of a grotesque stone figure.

clue.text: Showy food decoration had lost one point

indicators.note: having lost something means it is no longer there, so one letter drops out

parts.note: a garnish is a decorative touch on a plated dish
N is one compass point, north

explanation.surface: A flashy dish's garnish had lost some of its sparkle.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish means gaudy and loud in colour, a synonym of showy.

clue.text: Rogue coming from behind to discover a scallywag

indicators.note: the answer comes out of the run of letters in these words, sitting inside them

parts.note: the answer runs from the last letter of discover through a and into the start of scallywag

explanation.surface: A villain creeps up from behind to find a fellow rascal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scallywag' looks like the definition, but it holds the answer across its first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous scoundrel, a synonym of rogue.

clue.text: Call-girl spoken of in an obsequious way

parts.note: 'Oi!' is a rough call to attract someone's attention
Lily is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A prostitute is described as fawning and servile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call-girl' looks like one word, but it splits: shouting 'Oi!' at a girl named Lily.
explanation.definitionFit: Oily describes greasy, ingratiating flattery, so to act oilily is to behave in a fawning manner.

clue.text: Destruction of misplaced file is the end of everything

parts.note: loss can mean destruction, as of a ship
taken as written

indicators.note: misplaced means put in the wrong position, so the letters of file are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Losing an important computer file feels like the world ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Death is the end of everything for a person, and loss of life is a formal phrase for death.

clue.text: Sacred beetle's mark on seaman

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A holy beetle bears a mark on a sailor, perhaps as a tattoo.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has': the beetle has a mark followed by a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab was worshipped in ancient Egypt as a symbol of the sun god, hence a sacred insect.

clue.text: Joking jester in centre of Wigan

parts.note: a jester is a clown at court
taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: the five-letter town name has one middle letter, its third

explanation.surface: A funny entertainer performs in the middle of the Lancashire town of Wigan.
explanation.definitionFit: Clowning around is fooling and joking, so the two words share the sense of acting for laughs.

clue.text: Bypass round main street

parts.note: a ring is round in shape
a road is a main street

explanation.surface: A road that diverts traffic around a town's high street.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring road circles a town centre so traffic can avoid it, which is what a bypass does.

clue.text: This bean's a shiner

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... bean, a pale bean with a dark spot
second meaning: slang for a bruised eye after a punch

explanation.walkthrough: The 's links the two senses: the bean shares its name with a punched eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Black-eyed peas are often called black-eye beans, and a black eye is the bruise known as a shiner.

clue.text: Unsettled? Relax on the French ship!

parts.note: to rest is to relax
le is the French masculine 'the'
SS, steamship, prefixes ship names

explanation.surface: An uneasy passenger is told to unwind aboard a French vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless is agitated and cannot settle down, a direct synonym.

clue.text: No care wrecked part of eye

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed up, so these letters are broken and rebuilt

parts.note: the six letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Carelessness has damaged someone's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornea is the clear front layer covering the iris and pupil of the eye.

clue.text: Disease caused by tiny, quiet love-kiss

parts.note: small is a synonym of tiny
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
love is nil in tennis scoring, a zero shaped like O
X is the kiss written at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A sickness caught from one little peck on the lips.
explanation.definitionFit: Smallpox is a contagious viral illness, now eradicated, that left pockmarks on survivors.

clue.text: Obsessive person's coat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for a geek fixated on a dull hobby, like trainspotting
second meaning: a hooded waterproof jacket

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as the obsessive's own coat; it is a link. The slang sense comes from the hooded jackets worn by trainspotters.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a waterproof parka and, in British slang, a nerdy enthusiast.

clue.text: Exaggerated needlework?

definitions.meaning: the second sense of the answer: embellishment of a story beyond the truth
the literal sense: decorative stitching on cloth

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals a play on words: the same noun names fancy stitching and embellished storytelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Embroidery is ornamental sewing, and figuratively it is the adding of invented detail to a tale.

clue.text: Simple, Dr Watson!

definitions.meaning: the definition: something easy or basic
Sherlock Holmes's companion, the man Holmes famously addresses when calling a deduction easy

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes explains to his friend that the deduction was easy.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the first word of the famous line attributed to Holmes, though he never says it in Conan Doyle's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means basic or easy, the very word Holmes uses to dismiss a deduction as simple.

clue.text: Declines to drink, so brings dishonour to backward scholar

indicators.note: backward means turned around, so the degree letters are read in reverse

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
to stain someone's name is to disgrace it

explanation.surface: A teetotal academic refuses a drink and thereby shames a slow student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward scholar' looks like a dim pupil, but it means the graduate letters reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains refrains from alcohol, turning down the offer of a drink.

clue.text: Super ale brew gives enjoyment

indicators.note: to brew is to mix and stew ingredients, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A fine pint of beer brings delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is the feeling of satisfaction or delight, a direct synonym of enjoyment.

clue.text: Chief found in training over Northern fences

indicators.note: the answer is found in the run of letters spanning these words
the words fence in the answer, enclosing it within their letters

parts.note: the answer spans the last letter of training, all of over and the start of Northern

explanation.surface: A boss is spotted practising jumps over fences in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer begins at the last letter of 'training' and ends inside 'Northern'.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor is the head of a state, prison or school board, so he is the person in charge.

clue.text: William from the Far East produces menu

parts.note: Bill is a short form of the name William
of can mean from, as in 'a man of Kent'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called William brings a menu back from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill of fare is an old-fashioned name for a restaurant's list of dishes.

clue.text: Seafood swindler I am following

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the I comes after the rogue

parts.note: a scamp is a rascal or cheat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A con man trails someone through a fish restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are breaded langoustines, a popular British pub dish of shellfish.

clue.text: Extend sumptuous meal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stretch out or open fully
second meaning: a lavish feast laid out on a table

explanation.walkthrough: The verb and the noun are unrelated senses of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread is to stretch something out, and a spread is a generous array of food.

clue.text: Old bloke told about Spring

indicators.note: told means spoken, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: geezer is slang for a man, often an old one

explanation.surface: An elderly man hears about the springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season, but it is a hot spring of water. In British English the answer is pronounced like 'geezer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser is a hot spring that periodically erupts a column of water and steam.

clue.text: Merchant is backing red art

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the words red art are read from the end

parts.note: the six letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A dealer is supporting communist or crimson artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like a merchant financially supporting art, but it signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader is someone who buys and sells goods, a synonym of merchant.

clue.text: He believes I spliced badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to a poor splicing job, perhaps of film or rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower who believes in a teacher's doctrine, so 'he believes' describes one.

clue.text: Initially I go under a nasty African reptile

indicators.note: initially points to the starting letter of each of the words that follow

parts.words: I go under a nasty African
parts.note: the six words give their initial letters in order

explanation.surface: A speaker fears going down beneath some vicious African animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large lizard, and lizards are reptiles; it is an example of the class.

clue.text: Appear diminished, they say, but in one piece

indicators.note: they say flags that the words are heard rather than spelt, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to seem less is to appear diminished; said aloud it matches the answer

explanation.surface: Something looks smaller than before yet is still whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A seamless garment is made without joins, so it is all of one piece.

clue.text: Make a mistake about reserved wine

indicators.note: about means around, so the shy word is placed around the mistake word

parts.note: a shy person is reserved
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone blunders over which wine was set aside for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserved' looks like a booked bottle, but it means shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from the Jerez region of southern Spain.

clue.text: Roll found swirling in River Clyde

indicators.note: found means discovered sitting there, so the two letters are placed inside the jumbled river name
swirling water whirls around, so the letters of Clyde are mixed up

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A bread roll is discovered spinning in the Scottish River Clyde.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link here but two letters set inside the rearranged CLYDE; R for river then closes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller or drum is cylindrical, a solid with circular ends.
